Dashboard shows ingest stats, validation queue depth, archive counts
Validation inbox, search, and export views functional end-to-end | REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-006, REQ-008, REQ-009 | App | open | | REQ-012 | Observability foundation with structured logging, tracing, and metrics | OpenTelemetry tracing integrated across all backend services
Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint exposed
Structured logging routed through profile-driven log sink adapter | REQ-001 | Infra | open | ### Functional Scope — REQ-001 REQ-001 establishes the runtime profile adapter foundation that enables all subsequent REQs to operate identically across AWS and on-premises deployments. This is the architectural keystone for deployment portability as required by TECH_CONSTRAINTS. This REQ delivers a profile resolver that reads a runtime configuration (environment variable or config file) and selects the appropriate adapter implementations for five infrastructure concerns: object storage, message queue, event transport, secrets management, and log sink. Each concern is defined by a Python abstract interface (protocol/ABC) in the shared contracts module, with two concrete implementations — one for AWS services (S3, SQS, SNS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch) and one for on-prem equivalents (S3-compatible storage, approved queue broker, approved event transport, Vault/approved secret store, centralized log sink). The profile resolver is not a future adapter or placeholder. Both AWS and on-prem adapter implementations must be functional, testable, and usable by downstream REQs without modification. The AWS adapters use boto3/aiobotocore. The on-prem adapters use generic S3-compatible clients (e.g., MinIO SDK), generic queue clients, and generic HTTP/file-based fallbacks for secrets and logs. This REQ belongs to the broader scenario of ensuring that every business capability (ingest, processing, validation, archive, search, export, RAG) can be deployed on either profile without code changes to the application layer. Later REQs (REQ-004 through REQ-010) will import and use these adapter interfaces directly. What is delivered now: all five adapter interfaces, both profile implementations, profile resolver, configuration schema, and adapter contract tests. What is deferred: production-grade connection pooling tuning, circuit breaker policies, and cloud-specific IAM role configuration (these are operational concerns, not architectural gaps). ### Technical Scope — REQ-001 **Affected components:** `src/backend/shared/adapters/`, `src/backend/infra/profiles/`, `src/backend/infra/adapters/` **Main module boundary:** `src/backend/infra/` owns all adapter implementations. `src/backend/shared/adapters/` owns the abstract interfaces (protocols). **Canonical module family:** `backend.shared.adapters` for interfaces; `backend.infra.adapters.aws` and `backend.infra.adapters.onprem` for implementations; `backend.infra.profiles.resolver` for profile selection. **Integration points:** Environment variable `DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE` (values: `aws`, `onprem`) drives resolver. Each adapter is injected via FastAPI dependency injection. **Data contracts:** `ObjectStorageAdapter` (put_object, get_object, delete_object, presign_url), `QueueAdapter` (send_message, receive_messages, delete_message), `EventAdapter` (publish_event), `SecretsAdapter` (get_secret), `LogSinkAdapter` (emit_structured_log). All interfaces defined as Python Protocols with async methods. **Runtime expectations:** Both profiles must pass identical contract tests. AWS profile tested with localstack or moto in CI. On-prem profile tested with MinIO and in-memory queue/event stubs. **Configuration:** YAML or env-based config schema defining endpoints, credentials references, and region/zone for each profile. **Test expectations:** Contract tests for each adapter interface exercised against both implementations. At least one integration test per adapter per profile. Profile resolver unit tests for valid/invalid/missing profile values. **Candidate lane:** python. **Candidate domain:** enterprise. **Candidate runtime profile:** local-cloud. **Candidate skills:** backend-contract-boundary, local-cloud-parity. **Candidate packs:** enterprise-solution. **Gate expectations:** tests, lint, types, security, build. Coverage ≥ 80%. ### Acceptance — REQ-001 - Profile resolver correctly selects AWS adapters when `DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=aws` and on-prem adapters when `DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=onprem`. - Profile resolver raises a clear configuration error with actionable message when profile value is missing or invalid. - ObjectStorageAdapter interface is implemented for both AWS (S3 via boto3) and on-prem (S3-compatible via MinIO SDK), and both pass identical contract tests for put, get, delete, and presign operations. - QueueAdapter interface is implemented for both AWS (SQS) and on-prem (approved queue), and both pass identical contract tests for send, receive, and delete operations. - EventAdapter interface is implemented for both AWS (SNS) and on-prem (approved event transport), and both pass identical publish contract tests. - SecretsAdapter interface is implemented for both AWS (Secrets Manager) and on-prem (Vault-compatible), and both pass identical get_secret contract tests. - LogSinkAdapter interface is implemented for both AWS (CloudWatch-compatible structured output) and on-prem (centralized log sink structured output), and both pass identical emit contract tests. - All adapter interfaces are defined as Python Protocols in `src/backend/shared/adapters/` and are importable by downstream REQs without circular dependencies. - Configuration schema is documented and validated at startup; invalid configuration fails fast with structured error. - Unit and integration tests achieve ≥ 80% coverage for the infra adapter module. ### Out of Scope — REQ-001 - Production IAM role configuration or cloud-specific permission policies. - Circuit breaker, retry, or connection pool tuning beyond basic functional defaults. - Kubernetes manifests or Terraform/CDK infrastructure provisioning. - CI/CD pipeline configuration (deferred to operational setup). ### Future Compatibility — REQ-001 - All downstream REQs (REQ-002 through REQ-012) depend on the adapter interfaces defined here. These interfaces must remain stable. - The profile resolver pattern must be extensible to add new profiles (e.g., `edge`) without modifying existing adapter implementations. - Adapter interfaces must not leak profile-specific types into their signatures; all parameters and return types must be profile-agnostic. - FastAPI dependency injection pattern for adapter resolution must be documented so all later REQs follow the same injection approach. --- ### Functional Scope — REQ-002 REQ-002 establishes the canonical data contract backbone for the entire Zen 2030 platform. Every subsequent REQ that reads or writes document data, user references, audit records, or workflow state depends on the entity definitions, lifecycle enums, and migration infrastructure created here. This REQ defines the core domain entities: Document (with full lifecycle state machine), DocumentMetadata, ExtractedField, ValidationTask, ValidationDecision, ArchiveRecord, ExportJob, User (reference entity for RBAC), AuditLogEntry, and EmbeddingRecord (for future RAG). The Document entity carries a lifecycle state enum: `Uploaded → Processing → Extracted → InValidation → Validated → Archived → Exported`. State transitions are enforced at the model layer with explicit transition rules — invalid transitions raise domain errors. The REQ also enables the pgvector extension on PostgreSQL for future embedding storage (REQ-010) and creates the initial Alembic migration that establishes all tables, indexes, constraints, and the vector extension. What is delivered now: SQLAlchemy 2.0 models for all core entities, lifecycle state enum with transition validation, Alembic migration for initial schema, pgvector extension setup, and seed data for development. What is deferred: advanced indexing optimization, partitioning strategies, and production backup configuration. ### Technical Scope — REQ-002 **Affected components:** `src/backend/shared/models/`, `src/backend/shared/enums/`, `src/data/migrations/`, `src/data/schemas/` **Main module boundary:** `src/backend/shared/models/` owns all SQLAlchemy model definitions. `src/backend/shared/enums/` owns lifecycle state enums and transition rules. `src/data/migrations/` owns Alembic configuration and migration scripts. **Canonical module family:** `backend.shared.models` for entities; `backend.shared.enums` for domain enums; `data.migrations` for Alembic. **Integration points:** PostgreSQL 16 via SQLAlchemy 2.0 async engine. pgvector extension for vector columns. Alembic for migration management. **Data contracts:** - `Document`: id (UUID), title, original_filename, content_type, file_size_bytes, lifecycle_state (enum), uploaded_by (FK to User), uploaded_at, processed_at, validated_at, archived_at, classification_label, confidence_score, storage_key (object storage reference), created_at, updated_at. - `ExtractedField`: id, document_id (FK), field_name, field_value, confidence, extraction_method, created_at. - `ValidationTask`: id, document_id (FK), assigned_to (FK to User), status (pending/in_progress/completed), created_at, completed_at. - `ValidationDecision`: id, task_id (FK), decision (approved/rejected), corrected_fields (JSONB), reviewer_notes, decided_by (FK), decided_at. - `ArchiveRecord`: id, document_id (FK), storage_key, retention_until, archived_at. - `ExportJob`: id, document_ids (array), target_format, status (pending/processing/completed/failed), output_storage_key, requested_by (FK), created_at, completed_at. - `AuditLogEntry`: id, actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, details (JSONB), timestamp. - `EmbeddingRecord`: id, document_id (FK), chunk_index, chunk_text, embedding (vector), created_at. **Runtime expectations:** Migrations runnable against both AWS RDS PostgreSQL and on-prem PostgreSQL. pgvector extension must be available in both environments. **Test expectations:** Migration up/down tested. Model instantiation and state transition tests. Invalid state transition raises domain error. Seed data loads without errors. **Candidate lane:** sql + python. **Candidate domain:** enterprise. **Candidate runtime profile:** local-cloud. **Candidate skills:** backend-contract-boundary. **Candidate packs:** enterprise-solution. **Gate expectations:** tests, lint, types, build. ### Acceptance — REQ-002 - All core domain entities (Document, DocumentMetadata, ExtractedField, ValidationTask, ValidationDecision, ArchiveRecord, ExportJob, AuditLogEntry, EmbeddingRecord) are defined as SQLAlchemy 2.0 models in `src/backend/shared/models/`. - Document lifecycle state enum defines states Uploaded, Processing, Extracted, InValidation, Validated, Archived, Exported with explicit allowed transitions. - Attempting an invalid state transition (e.g., Uploaded → Validated) raises a domain error, not a silent no-op. - Alembic initial migration creates all tables, indexes, foreign keys, and enables pgvector extension. - Alembic migration is reversible (downgrade drops tables and extension cleanly). - EmbeddingRecord includes a vector column using pgvector with configurable dimensionality. - All models include created_at and updated_at timestamps with server defaults. - AuditLogEntry model supports JSONB details field for flexible audit payloads. - Seed data script creates at least one document in each lifecycle state for development testing. - Models are importable from `backend.shared.models` by all downstream REQs without circular dependencies. ### Out of Scope — REQ-002 - Table partitioning or advanced index optimization. - Production backup and restore procedures. - Read replica configuration. - Full-text search index creation (deferred to REQ-008). ### Future Compatibility — REQ-002 - All downstream REQs (REQ-004 through REQ-010) import entity models from `backend.shared.models`. These models must remain the single source of truth. - The lifecycle state enum and transition rules must remain stable. New states may be added but existing transitions must not be removed without migration. - The EmbeddingRecord schema must support REQ-010 without migration changes beyond adding indexes. - JSONB fields (ValidationDecision.corrected_fields, AuditLogEntry.details) must remain schema-flexible for future extension. --- ### Functional Scope — REQ-003 REQ-003 delivers the authentication and authorization foundation for the entire platform. Every API endpoint in subsequent REQs depends on the auth middleware and RBAC enforcement established here. This REQ implements OIDC-based authentication as the primary identity mechanism, with a SAML adapter seam for future federation. It defines three RBAC roles — Admin, Operator, Viewer — with explicit permission mappings. The auth middleware intercepts all API requests, validates OIDC tokens, resolves user identity and roles, and enforces role-based access on each endpoint. Unauthorized access attempts are denied with HTTP 403 and an audit log entry is created. The auth system is profile-independent: the same middleware works on both AWS and on-prem deployments. The OIDC provider endpoint is configured via the profile resolver (REQ-001). Token validation uses standard OIDC discovery and JWKS verification. What is delivered now: OIDC token validation middleware, RBAC role definitions and permission matrix, FastAPI dependency for role enforcement, audit logging of auth decisions, and SAML adapter interface (not full implementation). What is deferred: SAML full implementation, IdP group-to-role mapping UI, and session management beyond stateless JWT. ### Technical Scope — REQ-003 **Affected components:** `src/backend/auth/`, `src/backend/shared/models/` (User reference entity from REQ-002) **Main module boundary:** `src/backend/auth/` owns OIDC middleware, RBAC definitions, role enforcement dependencies, and auth adapter interfaces. **Canonical module family:** `backend.auth.middleware` for FastAPI middleware; `backend.auth.rbac` for role definitions and permission checks; `backend.auth.oidc` for OIDC token validation; `backend.auth.adapters` for SAML interface stub. **Integration points:** OIDC provider (Keycloak or compatible) via OIDC discovery URL configured per deployment profile. FastAPI dependency injection for `current_user` and `require_role(role)`. AuditLogEntry model from REQ-002 for auth event logging. **Data contracts:** - `AuthenticatedUser`: user_id, email, display_name, roles (list of Role enum), token_claims. - `Role` enum: Admin, Operator, Viewer. - Permission matrix: Admin (all operations), Operator (ingest, validate, search, export, Q&A), Viewer (search, read-only). - Auth deny response: HTTP 403 with structured error body and audit log entry. **Runtime expectations:** OIDC validation works with any compliant provider. For local development, a mock OIDC provider or test token generator is required. Both AWS and on-prem profiles configure the same OIDC discovery URL pattern. **Test expectations:** Unit tests for token validation (valid, expired, malformed, missing). Unit tests for RBAC permission checks per role. Integration test for middleware rejecting unauthenticated requests. Integration test for role-based endpoint access (allowed and denied). Audit log entry created on every deny. **Candidate lane:** python. **Candidate domain:** enterprise. **Candidate runtime profile:** local-cloud. **Candidate skills:** backend-contract-boundary, gate-risk-reviewer. **Candidate packs:** enterprise-solution. **Gate expectations:** tests, lint, types, security, build. Coverage ≥ 80%. ### Acceptance — REQ-003 - OIDC middleware validates JWT tokens using OIDC discovery and JWKS verification on every API request. - Requests with missing, expired, or malformed tokens receive HTTP 401 with structured error response. - RBAC roles Admin, Operator, Viewer are defined with explicit permission matrix documented in code. - `require_role` FastAPI dependency correctly allows access for authorized roles and denies with HTTP 403 for unauthorized roles. - Every HTTP 403 denial creates an AuditLogEntry with actor identity, attempted action, resource, and timestamp. - `current_user` FastAPI dependency extracts and returns AuthenticatedUser from validated token claims. - SAML adapter interface is defined in `backend.auth.adapters` as a Protocol, with a no-op stub implementation that raises NotImplementedError. - Auth middleware is profile-independent and works identically on AWS and on-prem deployments. - Local development includes a test token generator or mock OIDC provider configuration for testing without external IdP. - Unit and integration tests achieve ≥ 80% coverage for the auth module. ### Out of Scope — REQ-003 - Full SAML federation implementation (interface only). - IdP group-to-role mapping administration UI. - Session management, refresh token rotation, or token revocation beyond stateless JWT validation. - User provisioning or self-registration flows. ### Future Compatibility — REQ-003 - All downstream REQs (REQ-004 through REQ-011) use `current_user` and `require_role` dependencies. These must remain stable. - The Role enum may be extended with new roles but existing roles and their base permissions must not be removed. - The AuditLogEntry integration pattern (logging auth decisions) must be reusable for business-level audit in later REQs. - The SAML adapter interface must be implementable in a future REQ without changing the middleware or RBAC layer. --- ### Functional Scope — REQ-004 REQ-004 delivers the document ingest capability — the entry point for all documents into the Zen 2030 platform. Operators upload documents through an API endpoint, the system validates file type and size, stores the file in object storage via the profile adapter, persists document metadata to the database, and dispatches an ingest event to the processing queue for downstream OCR/IDP processing. This REQ supports all specified input formats: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, PNG. File validation rejects unsupported formats and oversized files with clear error messages. The document is created in `Uploaded` state and transitions to `Processing` when the queue message is confirmed sent. This is the first step in the end-to-end document journey: Upload → Process → Validate → Archive → Search/Export/Q&A. Without ingest, no downstream capability is exercisable. What is delivered now: upload API endpoint (multipart/form-data), file type and size validation, object storage persistence via adapter, database record creation, queue dispatch via adapter, and audit logging. What is deferred: batch upload, drag-and-drop UI (REQ-011), and duplicate detection. ### Technical Scope — REQ-004 **Affected components:** `src/backend/ingest/` **Main module boundary:** `src/backend/ingest/` owns the upload endpoint, file validation logic, and ingest orchestration. **Canonical module family:** `backend.ingest.router` for FastAPI route; `backend.ingest.service` for orchestration logic; `backend.ingest.validators` for file type/size validation. **Integration points:** ObjectStorageAdapter (REQ-001) for file persistence. QueueAdapter (REQ-001) for ingest event dispatch. Document model (REQ-002) for database record. Auth middleware (REQ-003) for Operator/Admin role enforcement. AuditLogEntry for ingest audit trail. **Data contracts:** - Upload request: multipart/form-data with file and optional metadata (title, tags). - Upload response: document_id (UUID), lifecycle_state, storage_key, created_at. - Ingest event message: `{document_id, storage_key, content_type, uploaded_by, uploaded_at}`. - Validation rules: allowed content types (application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.*, image/jpeg, image/png), max file size configurable (default 100MB). **Runtime expectations:** Works identically on AWS and on-prem via adapter injection. File stored to S3 or S3-compatible storage. Event dispatched to SQS or approved queue. **Test expectations:** Happy path: upload valid PDF, verify document created in Uploaded state, file in object storage, event in queue. Reject: unsupported file type returns 400. Reject: oversized file returns 413. Auth: unauthenticated upload returns 401. Auth: Viewer role upload returns 403. Failure: object storage failure rolls back database record. Audit: successful and failed uploads logged. **Candidate lane:** python. **Candidate domain:** enterprise. **Candidate runtime profile:** local-cloud. **Candidate skills:** backend-contract-boundary. **Candidate packs:** enterprise-solution. **Gate expectations:** tests, lint, types, security, build. Coverage ≥ 80%. ### Acceptance — REQ-004 - Upload endpoint accepts multipart/form-data POST with file and optional metadata, returns document_id and lifecycle_state. - All six supported formats (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, PNG) are accepted and stored successfully. - Unsupported file types are rejected with HTTP 400 and a structured error message naming the rejected content type. - Files exceeding the configured maximum size are rejected with HTTP 413. - Uploaded file is persisted to object storage via ObjectStorageAdapter with a unique storage key. - Document record is created in the database in `Uploaded` state with all required metadata fields populated. - Ingest event is dispatched to the processing queue via QueueAdapter with document_id, storage_key, and content_type. - Document transitions from `Uploaded` to `Processing` after queue dispatch confirmation. - Only users with Operator or Admin role can upload; Viewer role receives HTTP 403 with audit log entry. - Object storage failure during upload results in no orphaned database record (transactional rollback or compensation). - Every upload attempt (success or failure) creates an AuditLogEntry. ### Out of Scope — REQ-004 - Batch upload of multiple files in a single request. - Duplicate detection or deduplication logic. - Frontend upload UI (deferred to REQ-011). - Virus/malware scanning (operational concern, not application logic). ### Future Compatibility — REQ-004 - The ingest event message schema must remain stable for REQ-005 (processing pipeline consumer). - The storage_key format must be compatible with REQ-007 (archive) and REQ-009 (export) retrieval patterns. - The upload endpoint response schema must be compatible with REQ-011 (frontend upload form). --- ### Functional Scope — REQ-005 REQ-005 delivers the OCR and IDP processing pipeline that transforms uploaded documents into structured, classified, field-extracted records ready for human validation. This is the automated intelligence layer of the platform. A queue consumer listens for ingest events (from REQ-004), retrieves the document file from object storage, and runs it through a configurable processing pipeline: OCR (Tesseract + PaddleOCR/docTR), parsing (Apache Tika + Unstructured), classification (configurable rules plus optional layout-aware models), and field extraction. Results are persisted as ExtractedField records linked to the document. The document transitions to `Extracted` state on success or `Error` state on failure. The pipeline is designed to be extensible: each processing step is a pluggable component behind an interface, allowing future replacement of OCR engines or classification models without changing the orchestration logic. What is delivered now: queue consumer, OCR integration, parsing integration, classification engine, field extraction, result persistence, state transitions, error handling with retry. What is deferred: custom model training, advanced layout analysis, and processing performance optimization. ### Technical Scope — REQ-005 **Affected components:** `src/backend/processing/` **Main module boundary:** `src/backend/processing/` owns the queue consumer, pipeline orchestrator, and processing step implementations. **Canonical module family:** `backend.processing.consumer` for queue listener; `backend.processing.pipeline` for orchestration; `backend.processing.steps.ocr`, `backend.processing.steps.parsing`, `backend.processing.steps.classification`, `backend.processing.steps.extraction` for individual steps. **Integration points:** QueueAdapter (REQ-001) for consuming ingest events. ObjectStorageAdapter (REQ-001) for retrieving document files. Document and ExtractedField models (REQ-002) for persistence. Each processing step defined as a Protocol for pluggability. **Data contracts:** - Ingest event consumed: `{document_id, storage_key, content_type, uploaded_by, uploaded_at}`. - OCR output: raw text per page. - Parsing output: structured sections, tables, metadata. - Classification output: label, confidence_score. - Extraction output: list of `{field_name, field_value, confidence, extraction_method}`. - All results persisted as ExtractedField records. **Runtime expectations:** Processing runs as a background worker (can be same container or separate). OCR libraries (Tesseract, PaddleOCR) must be available in container image. Works on both AWS and on-prem via adapter injection. **Test expectations:** Happy path: process a sample PDF, verify ExtractedFields created and document in Extracted state. Error path: corrupt file results in Error state with error details logged. Retry: transient queue failure retries message. Idempotency: reprocessing same document_id does not create duplicate ExtractedFields. Each processing step testable in isolation via Protocol interface. **Candidate lane:** python. **Candidate domain:** enterprise. **Candidate runtime profile:** local-cloud. **Candidate skills:** backend-contract-boundary. **Candidate packs:** enterprise-solution. **Gate expectations:** tests, lint, types, security, build. Coverage ≥ 80%. ### Acceptance — REQ-005 - Queue consumer successfully receives and processes ingest events from the processing queue. - Document file is retrieved from object storage via ObjectStorageAdapter using the storage_key from the ingest event. - OCR step extracts text from PDF and image documents using Tesseract (with PaddleOCR/docTR as configurable alternative). - Parsing step extracts structured content from DOCX, XLSX, PPTX using Apache Tika / Unstructured. - Classification step assigns a classification label and confidence score to the document. - Extraction step produces ExtractedField records with field_name, field_value, confidence, and extraction_method. - Document transitions to `Extracted` state after successful processing with all results persisted. - Document transitions to `Error` state when processing fails, with error details stored in an audit log entry. - Reprocessing the same document_id is idempotent — existing ExtractedFields are replaced, not duplicated. - Each processing step implements a shared Protocol interface and is independently testable. -
